cases.alertTitle: Unsigned binary beaconing from a build agent
cases.detectionRule: EDR · unsigned image with fixed-interval outbound

evidence.detail: The binary's parent is the build-agent service itself, with no pipeline job in the lineage — nothing scheduled it.
evidence.label: Spawned by the agent service, not a job

evidence.detail: Outbound every 47 seconds to a domain registered four days ago, with no other host in the estate talking to it.
evidence.label: Fixed-interval outbound to a young domain

evidence.detail: No change ticket, maintenance window or engagement covers BLD-AGENT-03 this week.
evidence.label: No change record

learn.concept: Containment urgency is a property of the ASSET as much as the alert: a host that signs or distributes artefacts is contained first and triaged second.
learn.pointer: Fixture-only case — it exists to reach the under-contained branch.

cases.trigger: An unsigned binary on BLD-AGENT-03 has been reaching the same external host on a fixed interval since 03:40.
cases.why: Live, unauthorized code with a live channel out of a build host is contain-now: the build agent signs artefacts the whole estate trusts. Handing it to Tier-2 without containment leaves the channel open while the ticket queues, which is the under-contained call this fixture exists to grade.

cases.alertTitle: Bulk export by an account already under review
cases.detectionRule: DLP · volume anomaly on a flagged account

evidence.detail: 4.2 GB against a 90-day median of 60 MB, all from one folder, in one sitting.
evidence.label: Volume far above the user's own baseline

evidence.detail: HR opened a conduct review on 4 June. No leaving date is recorded.
evidence.label: Open review, no departure date

evidence.detail: The egress lands in a consumer storage account, not the corporate tenant.
evidence.label: Destination is a personal account

learn.concept: Insider cases are escalated, not contained unilaterally: the evidence chain and the employment process both break if the subject learns they are being watched.
learn.pointer: Fixture-only case — it exists to grade an acceptable-but-not-exact escalation.

cases.trigger: mokoro exported 4.2 GB from the deal room at 22:10, a week after HR opened a review.
cases.why: This is real, unauthorized movement of company data, so it escalates — but an insider under an open HR review belongs with Tier-2, HR and legal before a single analyst isolates the person's device. Isolation is defensible here, which is exactly why this case carries it as an acceptable call.

cases.alertTitle: Encoded PowerShell during a patch window

evidence.detail: The lineage is the patch-management agent, running as its own service account — the estate's normal deployment path.
evidence.label: Parent is the management agent

evidence.detail: The decoded block reads local package versions and writes them to the management server. Nothing leaves the estate.
evidence.label: Decodes to an inventory query

evidence.detail: CHG-5104 names PATCH-RELAY-02, the agent and the 02:00–04:00 window, approved by the platform team.
evidence.label: CHG-5104 covers the window

learn.concept: Encoding is not the threat; the sanction artifact is the discriminator. A named change ticket turns a correct detection into a benign true positive without touching the rule's logic.
learn.pointer: Fixture-only case — it exists to grade a Benign-TP with no acceptable alternatives.

cases.trigger: An encoded PowerShell command ran on PATCH-RELAY-02 at 02:05, inside the monthly maintenance window.
cases.why: The behaviour the rule hunts for really happened — encoded PowerShell ran — and a named change ticket sanctions it. That is a Benign True Positive: the detection is right and the activity is authorized. Closing it as a false positive would tell the next analyst the rule misfired, and it did not.
